title: Remote access
subtitle: SSH, keys, scp, bastion, config, and SFTP

cards.meaning: Keyboard and screen on the machine; still needed when network/SSH is down
cards.notes: Daily admin is usually remote, not at the console.

cards.meaning: Unencrypted remote login — credentials and session travel in the clear
cards.notes: Legacy only. Do not use on a real network. Postcard vs SSH sealed envelope.

cards.meaning: Encrypted shell, remote commands, port forwarding, and file transfer (SCP/SFTP)
cards.notes: Default for Linux remote access.

cards.meaning: Program for login and remote commands (OpenSSH on Linux/macOS; PuTTY on Windows)
Windows GUI file manager for remote copying over SSH (SFTP/SCP)
cards.notes: Browse/drag files without remembering scp syntax.

cards.meaning: Network-transparent GUI: app (X client) can run remote; display (X server) on your laptop
cards.notes: Often tunneled through SSH with X11 forwarding. One GUI program over the network.

cards.meaning: Full remote desktop: VNC server on the machine, VNC client on yours
cards.notes: Whole desktop, not one application window.

cards.meaning: Generate an RSA key pair on your machine
cards.notes: -t rsa = RSA key type. Creates ~/.ssh if missing.

cards.meaning: Private identification key — never distribute
cards.notes: Default path from ssh-keygen. OpenSSH refuses group/world-readable keys.

cards.meaning: Public key — copy this to servers
cards.notes: .pub travels; id_rsa never leaves your control.

cards.meaning: Private key usable without typing a phrase — convenient, weaker if laptop is stolen
cards.notes: Non-empty = extra decrypt step before SSH can use the key.

cards.meaning: Short hash so you can recognize this key later (known_hosts, audit)
Owner read/write only; required so OpenSSH will use the private key
cards.notes: Same idea for ~/.ssh/config.

cards.meaning: Private key file location
cards.notes: Cloud images often use *.pem instead of id_rsa.

cards.meaning: Remote user to log in as (same idea as user@host)
Remote SSH port (default 22)
cards.notes: scp uses capital -P for port.

cards.meaning: Force pseudo-terminal allocation
cards.notes: Needed for screen-based menus and sudo. Multiple -t even if ssh has no local tty.

cards.meaning: Verbose mode — debug auth and connection
cards.notes: Repeat for more detail: -vv, -vvv.

cards.meaning: Do not execute a remote command — tunnel/port-forward only
cards.notes: Keeps the tunnel open without a shell.

cards.meaning: On the remote account: holds public key lines that may log in
cards.notes: Append contents of local id_rsa.pub — do not overwrite existing keys.

cards.meaning: Forbidden by default on most systems
cards.notes: Allowing it: edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config (e.g. PermitRootLogin) and restart sshd. Prefer user + sudo.

cards.meaning: sshd settings: root login, SFTP jail, ports, Match blocks, …
cards.notes: Always systemctl restart sshd after edits. Keep a console session open.

cards.meaning: Run one command remotely without an interactive shell
Local shell sees ; — pwd/ls may run locally after ssh finishes whoami
cards.notes: Quote the remote string if everything must run on the server.

cards.meaning: Feed a local script to the remote shell via stdin
Often fails: sudo must be run from a terminal
cards.notes: Enable with -t.

cards.meaning: Copy files over SSH (same auth as ssh)
cards.notes: Form: scp source destination. Colon after host starts the remote path.

cards.meaning: Port for scp — capital P, unlike ssh’s -p
Copy local file into a remote directory
Copy remote file into the current local directory
cards.notes: . = here.

cards.meaning: Copy between two remotes; traffic goes through your machine
Public-subnet jump server to reach private instances with no public IP
cards.notes: Linux: SSH. Windows: RDP. Two keys, two users (bastion + private VM).

cards.meaning: Instead of direct TCP, jump box forwards stdio to target host (%h) and port (%p)
cards.example: ssh -i lab.pem -o "ProxyCommand ssh -W %h:%p -i key_for_jumpbox.pem jumpbox_user@jump.box.host" centos@target
cards.notes: Outer ssh uses target key; inner ssh uses jumpbox key.

cards.meaning: Per-user SSH aliases: HostName, User, Port, IdentityFile, ProxyJump, …
cards.notes: chmod 600 — it can list IdentityFile paths.

cards.meaning: Host = alias you type; HostName = real IP/DNS
cards.example:
Host targaryen
    HostName 192.168.1.10
    User daenerys
    Port 7654
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/targaryen.key
cards.notes: ssh targaryen equals the long -i/-p/user@ command.

cards.meaning: FTP = old unencrypted; SFTP = SSH file protocol (encrypted, usually port 22)
Interactive secure file transfer over SSH
cards.notes: Clients may also support SCP, plain FTP, batch scripting, editor, directory sync.

cards.meaning: Following sshd_config lines apply only to that user
No shell — only the internal SFTP server
cards.notes: SFTP-only drop-box account.

cards.meaning: After login the user cannot see above this directory
Lock down SFTP-only user: not a jump box or X client
cards.example:
PermitTunnel no
AllowAgentForwarding no
AllowTcpForwarding no
X11Forwarding no

cards.meaning: Apply /etc/ssh/sshd_config changes
cards.notes: Needed after root login, SFTP jail, ports, Match blocks, … Bad config can lock you out.
